title: Opaque metering bundle and uplink protocol for on-prem usage reporting
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: design and implement an opaque, auditable export bundle format and uplink protocol for Private/VPC and air-gapped on-prem deployments so usage counters, rate-limit deltas, and quota reconciliations can be verified server-side after delayed sync. Scope: exporter service on on-prem collector, bundle signing and watermarking, resumable transfer API for gateway, server-side idempotent ingestion, reconciliation job, local retention/rotation policy, and operator runbook. This ticket covers the bundle format, edge uploader prototyping, ingestion idempotency semantics, and acceptance criteria for correctness under delayed sync and partial retries.
acceptance_criteria: On-prem collector can produce compact daily bundles containing per-customer usage events (generation tokens, embedding units, API calls) for a configurable lookback window and compress them into signed archives.
Bundles include sequence watermarks, per-tenant monotonically-increasing counters, and chunk-level checksums so server can validate completeness and detect missing ranges.
Server-side ingestion endpoint supports resumable multi-chunk upload with content-addressed chunks and guarantees idempotent application of usage deltas (retries and duplicates do not double-count).
Reconciliation job can reconcile delayed bundles older than 7 days and produce an audit report with discrepancies > 0.1% flagged and traced to bundle IDs and chunk offsets.

Rate-limiter state and quota usage derived from offline bundles match live telemetry within defined tolerances after replay; unit tests and integration test harness validate edge cases (out-of-order bundles, partial uploads, signer key rotation).

Security: bundles are signed with customer-provided key (or Redwood-managed key) and server rejects unsigned or wrongly-signed bundles. Documentation and runbook exist for key rotation and emergency key revocation.
implementation_notes: Bundle format: newline-delimited JSON events + minimal header with bundle_id, tenant_id, start_seq, end_seq, created_at, signer_id. Produce optional binary sidecar for large KV cache dumps.
Chunking: 8MB chunks with SHA256 checksum per chunk and manifest file mapping chunk->byte-range for resumable upload.
Signing: support ECDSA P-256 signatures; include signer_id and public key fingerprint in header. Verify on ingest and store signer metadata in audit table.

Ingestion API: /v1/private/usage/uplink/manifest to register manifest; /v1/private/usage/uplink/chunk to upload chunks; finalise call triggers validation and apply. All calls are idempotent using manifest_id + chunk_index keys.
Server apply semantics: compute delta = max(0, reported_counter - last_seen_counter) per tenant+metric; persist ledger entries with bundle_id and chunk_range to enable future reversibility.
Backfill/replay: implement reconcile worker that runs periodic replays, verifies checksum and sequence continuity, and emits anomaly events to billing-dashboard and PagerDuty if gaps found.
Telemetry: emit metrics for bundle validation success rate, chunk retries, size distribution, apply latency, and reconcile mismatches. Add dashboard widgets to billing console.
Operator config: local retention policy default 90 days; config knobs for chunk size, max bundle size, and retry window. Provide safe defaults for resource constrained on-prem devices.
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing, chunk checksum validation, and signature verification.
Integration tests: simulate out-of-order uploads, duplicate chunks, partial manifests, and interrupted transfers; verify idempotency and correct delta calculation.
Staging run: deploy collector binary to staging on-prem VM with synthetic traffic generator that emits controlled counters; produce bundles and run full uplink->ingest->reconcile flow.
Chaos experiment: drop random chunk uploads and resume; verify reconcile detects and recovers; measure time-to-repair metrics.
Load test: ingest 10k bundles/day across 100 tenants to validate apply throughput and ledger table performance; ensure no deadlocks or long-running transactions.
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (canary): enable bundle generation and upload for internal test tenants only. Monitor apply success rate and reconcile alerts.
Phase 2 (pilot): invite 5 customers with Private deployment to opt-in. Provide on-call support and runbook walkthrough.
Phase 3 (general): flip default to enabled for all on-prem collectors; publish operator upgrade notes and key-rotation checklist.
Fallback: if ingestion fails for a tenant, mark tenant as 'delayed_sync' and keep serving from live counters; surface clear dashboard warnings and contact CS.
comments: 2025-02-13 — Ava Chen: initial RFC posted to Confluence (link below). Decided to prefer signed bundles over TLS-only push to allow air-gapped handoffs. Asked security to review signer key model.
2025-02-18 — Priya Nair (Billing): reviewed acceptance criteria — asked for explicit idempotency guarantee and auditability for charge disputes. Added reconciliation threshold requirement.

2025-02-20 — Diego Ramos (Infra): prototype for resumable chunk upload done; observed high memory pressure when encoding large KV sidecars. Suggested streaming compression and smaller default chunk size for older on-prem machines.
2025-02-25 — Marcus Lee: implemented manifest registration endpoint. Next: chunk upload and server-side apply with ledger writes. Will open PRs and link here.

2025-02-28 — Security review (Lena Ortiz): raised threat about key rotation and signing algorithm lifetime. Recommend supporting dual-signing during rotation window and storing signer fingerprints in secure KVS.
